title: Power of two is not enough

title: Cube counts
stem: How many syntactically distinct cubes of n variables have exactly k free coordinates? How many cubes exist in total?
solution:
**Derivation and interpretation.** Choose the k free positions in $\binom nk$ ways, then assign each remaining position either zero or one in $2^{n-k}$ ways. The count is $\binom nk2^{n-k}$. For n=4, the counts for k=0,1,2,3,4 are 16,32,24,8,1 and total 81. The number of Boolean functions is instead $2^{2^n}$, because each truth-table row chooses an independent output. title: Parity lower bound

title: Threshold lower bound

title: Static-one hazard
